newsitem.headline: UK CBI Dec monthly trends survey -- table.

text.p: survey of trends in UK manufacturing by the Confederation of
CBI MONTHLY TRENDS ENQUIRY (a) DEC NOV OCT SEPT
NOTES - * over the coming four months;
The survey was conducted between November 22 and December 9.
1,222 manufacturing companies responded, representing 50 industries and accounting for about half of the UK's manufactured exports and output of some two million employees;
- (a) in percent, giving balance between those replying "up', "above normal' or "more than adequate,' and those replying "down', "below normal" or "less than adequate."
The CBI said demand from overseas has weakened, leaving the balance of export order books at their lowest level since February 1994.

"The weakening in export demand is not surprising as our survey was conducted against a backdrop of the rising value of sterling. However, home demand for manufactured goods continues to hold up," said Sudhir Junankar, associate director of economic analysis at the CBI.
"The pick-up expected in domestic prices is now becoming more firmly based, suggesting that a turning point in output price inflation is at hand."
